paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when everything looks finished, God is not finished. Jesus is dead, the stone is rolled, and Joseph goes away (Matthew 27:60). The story is not over, and this passage is built to make you feel how closed that tomb looks so you can see how much bigger God is than a closed door.

Look at what the chief priests and Pharisees say. They remember that Jesus said, "After three days I will rise again" (Matthew 27:63). Think about that, friend! His own words were remembered by the people who called Him a deceiver, and their worry, they told Pilate, was that the disciples would steal Him away and tell the people He had risen, so they went and sealed the stone and posted the guard (Matthew 27:64, 66).

So what does that mean for you? The words of Jesus are worth remembering, because even the people who opposed Him couldn't forget them. Joseph and the two women show up and do the small, faithful thing in the dark (Matthew 27:57-61), and so can you when the day looks like a closed tomb. Keep your ovens ready, baker. This story is NOT over.
